_comment: Architectural component mapping for CodeScene's inter-module coupling and architectural
decay analysis. These components mirror the boundaries enforced as tests in
tests/PoRedoImage.Tests.Architecture/ArchitectureRules.cs - the same model measured two ways:
NetArchTest answers 'is the boundary violated right now?' (binary, build-gating), CodeScene
answers 'are these components drifting toward each other over time?' (trend, advisory).
Keep the two in step: adding a feature slice means adding it in both places.

components.name: Domain
components._role: Entities and interfaces. Depends on nothing; every arrow points inward to here.

components.name: Application
components._role: Use cases and agents. May depend on Domain and Shared only.

components.name: Infrastructure
components._role: AI providers, storage, caching decorators. Implements Domain abstractions.

components.name: Shared-Contracts
components._role: DTOs and validation crossing the WASM/API boundary. Must stay trim-safe.

components.name: Web-BFF
components._role: API/BFF host and vertical feature slices. Composition root.

components.name: Client-WASM
components._role: The only assembly shipped to the browser. All interactive UI.

components.name: Mobile-MAUI
components._role: Android head. Talks to the API over HTTP; holds no provider keys.

components.name: Tests
components._role: All four-plus test tiers. Separated so test churn does not read as product decay.

_comment: Pairs CodeScene should treat as EXPECTED coupling (they share a deliberate contract), so
that change-coupling between them is not reported as architectural decay. Everything not
listed is unexpected coupling and worth a look.
_forbidden_rationale: Client-WASM <-> Infrastructure and Client-WASM <-> Web-BFF are absent deliberately: server
code must never ship to the browser. NetArchTest gates those as hard rules
(client-no-infrastructure, client-no-web); CodeScene surfacing change-coupling there would
be an early warning that someone is about to break one.
